newsitem.title: POLAND: No firm decision on Polish fuel prices yet - finmin.
newsitem.headline: No firm decision on Polish fuel prices yet - finmin.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday reviewed one possible scenario for the freeing of fuel prices but it made no firm decisions, the finance ministry spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

Grazyna Kowalska told Reuters that even if the government were to set a date for freeing of prices, which are now controlled by the finance ministry, it would be kept secret because of the impact it could have on the market.

"The meeting yesterday was neither the first nor the last (on fuel price freeing). The government is trying to find a way which would be the least harmful to the market and it will take some time yet," she said.
"(On Tuesday) the government reviewed one of the options but no firm decisions have been made. They will be made at the most suitable time from the point of view of the market," she said.
Late on Tuesday PAP news agency quoted an anonymous, senior government official as saying the cabinet had already decided on the timetable and method of freeing fuel prices.

Government caps on domestic fuel prices have seriously cut the profits of Poland's refineries, which have had to buy crude oil at world prices and sell their products at the maximum prices set by the ministry.

The freeing of fuel prices is the key to the restructuring of Poland's oil sector which will lead to the privatisation of refineries. The issue was not on the government's formal agenda for its Tuesday session.
